items.title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
items.summary: OpenAI says an AI system it built solved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems, after running for 88 hours across 10,000 of its AI systems and spending millions of dollars. OpenAI published a formal proof in Lean alongside a write-up. The claim has triggered a backlash from mathematicians, including a NYU mathematician who accused OpenAI of fighting dirty, with academics disputing the announcement's validity and provenance.
items.why_it_matters: If verified, it would be the most dramatic evidence yet that frontier AI can produce genuinely new mathematics, but the credibility fight shows how contested AI-generated proofs remain.

items.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: A predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome
items.summary: Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome Atlas, a predictive map estimating the molecular effects of roughly 9 billion possible single-letter DNA variants across the entire human genome.
items.why_it_matters: A comprehensive predictive map of genetic variation could accelerate research into disease mechanisms and new treatments.

items.title: Mistral raises €3B as sovereign AI becomes big business
items.summary: French AI lab Mistral raised €3 billion (about $3.5 billion) in a Series D round led by Samsung Electronics, along with Scaleup Europe and PSG Equity, valuing the company at roughly €21 billion (about $24 billion). CEO Arthur Mensch said Mistral remains undervalued and argued open-source models are gaining the upper hand; Samsung separately announced a strategic partnership with Mistral to strengthen its AI chip engineering and manufacturing capabilities.
items.why_it_matters: It's one of the largest funding rounds ever for a European AI lab, reinforcing Mistral's role as the leading challenger to US and Chinese frontier labs.

items.title: Introducing Muse: The World’s First Personal AI Agent Built for Everyone
items.summary: Meta launched Muse, which it calls the world's first personal AI agent, designed to proactively help users meet goals, manage tasks, and connect with WhatsApp and Instagram, including sending emails and booking travel. The launch comes as Meta faces a broader public reckoning over privacy and safety in its push into personal AI agents.
items.why_it_matters: It puts Meta squarely in competition for the emerging personal AI agent category against OpenAI and Google, while testing how much users will trust an AI agent with their private communications.

items.title: Early Data Indicates an A.I.-Generated Drug Could Slow Aging
items.summary: Techbio company Insilico Medicine reported early data suggesting rentosertib, an AI-designed drug candidate originally developed for a rare lung condition, also reduces biological markers of aging. Co-CEO Alex Zhavoronkov said he has similar hopes for the company's broader pipeline of AI-discovered drugs, including one targeting fibrosis.
items.why_it_matters: It's an early but notable sign that AI-driven drug discovery can produce candidates with real, measurable biological effects beyond their original target.

items.title: ASML, TSMC, Samsung, Intel Back 12-Inch Masks for AI Chips
items.summary: ASML won commitments from TSMC, Samsung, and Intel to adopt its newest High NA EUV lithography tools and back a broader shift to 12-inch photomask production, as chipmakers race to meet surging demand for more powerful AI chips. Samsung separately said it is expanding its long-standing manufacturing partnership with ASML on High NA EUV technology.
items.why_it_matters: It shows the world's top chipmakers coordinating investment in next-generation manufacturing capacity to keep pace with AI-driven chip demand.

items.title: Meta Ran Hundreds of Ads Showing AI Child Sexual Abuse, NGO Says
items.summary: Meta ran more than 300 advertisements on Instagram and Facebook containing suspected child sexual abuse material this year, according to a report from the nonprofit Tech Transparency Project, which found ads promoting apps that "nudify" real photos of young girls. Reporting found Meta was slow to remove the ads after they were flagged.
items.why_it_matters: It underscores how AI-powered 'nudifying' apps are being used to generate child abuse imagery and raises pressure on platforms to police AI-driven ad content.

items.title: Qualcomm issues warrants to Amazon to acquire $4 billion worth of chipmaker's stock as part of AI infrastructure deal
items.summary: Qualcomm signed Amazon as a data center chip customer in a multi-generation AI infrastructure deal, issuing Amazon warrants to acquire up to $4 billion worth of Qualcomm stock. The agreement gives Amazon another source of custom AI chips beyond Nvidia and marks a major win for Qualcomm's push into the data center market.
items.why_it_matters: It signals growing diversification away from Nvidia's dominance in AI chips and deepens the financial ties between major cloud and chip providers.

items.title: A Hacking Tool Built With A.I. Can Breach Phones Without a Click
items.summary: AI researchers discovered a hacking tool, built with AI, that could breach phones without any click from the victim; researchers said the attack could have compromised hundreds of millions of devices within hours.
items.why_it_matters: It shows AI can be used to discover and potentially automate high-severity, zero-click security exploits at scale.

items.title: How a Blacklisted Chinese Tech Giant Kept Buying America’s Best A.I. Chips
items.summary: Despite US sanctions imposed on Chinese tech giant Inspur over its work with the Chinese military, a subsidiary of the company kept shipping Nvidia's best AI chips to leading Chinese AI firms.
items.why_it_matters: It exposes gaps in US export controls meant to keep advanced AI chips out of sanctioned Chinese firms' hands.
